correctness.rationale: All-valuation counterexample for differing neighbourhoods of distance-two non-neighbours forces complete multipartiteness; converse directly checks every neighbour and each part case. A bridge in complete multipartite graphs implies star; deleting a nonbridge edge is safe exactly for distinct singleton parts, adding within a part only if its size is two, and adding across components only for isolate-to-star-center or isolate-to-isolate. The labelled exponential formula and edge-toggle involution prove both marked EGFs. A separate standard-library implementation exhausts 33868 labelled graphs through n=6, 2131019 valuations and 24796 valid-graph edit cases; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: Preservation of modal frame-validity under one accessibility change is a natural robustness question. The theorem determines precise safe-edge locations for every finite component-size profile and all-size weighted labelled counts, beyond the known yes/no general-frame correspondence or basic unmarked Bell counts. The two-deletion/three-insertion mechanisms and reversible aggregate counting are mathematically interpretable and reusable.
